name: Endoscopic carpal tunnel approach
corridor: System-specific endoscopic visualization of the undersurface of the transverse carpal ligament

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm supported on a hand table and the wrist accessible for the selected system.

setup.text: Confirm the endoscopic system, supervising surgeon's portal and trajectory, and an open-conversion plan before starting.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the wrist crease and the system-specific portal landmarks selected by the supervising surgeon.

incision.text: Create the system-specific portal under direct supervision; device-specific steps require formal system training.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the intended portal path without forcing instruments through resistance or uncertain anatomy.

deep_interval.text: Obtain an unobstructed view of the undersurface of the transverse carpal ligament before activating a cutting element.

layers.text: Portal, distal forearm fascia as applicable, carpal-tunnel path, then the undersurface of the transverse carpal ligament.

structures_encountered.text: The transverse carpal ligament is visualized with the median nerve and flexor tendons deep and the superficial palmar arch distal.

structures_at_risk.text: Protect the median nerve and recurrent motor branch, flexor tendons, superficial palmar arch, and ulnar neurovascular structures.

danger_zones.text: Do not cut with inadequate visualization, bleeding, synovial obstruction, anomalous anatomy, or an uncertain distal endpoint.

retraction_hazards.text: Never force the scope or instruments when the intended plane cannot be maintained confidently.

exposure.text: The endoscopic approach visualizes the ligament from within the selected system's controlled path.

limitations.text: Visualization and safe completion depend on anatomy, hemostasis, surgeon training, and the selected device system.

extensions.text: Convert to open release when visualization, orientation, hemostasis, or completeness cannot be demonstrated safely.

indications.text: Use when endoscopic release is selected based on patient factors, surgeon expertise, equipment, and ability to visualize the ligament safely.

relative_contraindications.text: Do not continue endoscopically when safe ligament identification or visualization cannot be maintained.

closure.text: Confirm the release endpoint and hemostasis before portal closure and dressing.

complications.text: Failure modes include incomplete release, nerve or tendon injury, vascular injury, hematoma, infection, pillar pain, and conversion-related delay.

bailouts.text: Stop cutting and convert to open release when visualization or safe completion is uncertain.

questions.question: When should endoscopic release be converted?
questions.answer: When safe ligament identification, visualization, hemostasis, or confirmation of complete release cannot be maintained.

questions.question: What must be seen before activating the cutting element?
questions.answer: An unobstructed view of the undersurface of the transverse carpal ligament within the intended system-specific path.
